I would actually advise against having both a media server AND minecraft server on one machine. Especially if you are using Plex. Plex will be encoding on the fly any video that will be displayed on a resolution that the video was not made in (ie. if the video is 1080p but you are streaming to a tablet, it will encode the video in real time to the size of the tablet). Doing that will make a huge performance hit on the minecraft server. Not to mention, the streaming from the server will also eat up the bandwidth.

You wouldn't have the problem with Kodi since Kodi doesn't stream, just outputs. But, if you have Kodi running, THAT is your UI. Management of the minecraft will have to be done via ssh.

If you really are hell bent on having both on one machine, I would go with either Debian or Ubuntu server edition. Install Kodi and the minecraft server. Leave Kodi on all the time and have minecraft manageable from ssh.

In linux mint it is dead simple to change the text size to make it larger, and it helps if you set the tv as your primary monitor and choose its native resolution (the program for this is simply called Display).

Unfortunately televisions and monitors are surprisingly different. You are usually no more than two feet from a monitor, but the average distance from a television is closer to 5-7 feet because of that the pixels are larger and further apart.

Bottom line, unless you have some specialty 4K or UltraHD TV the picture will look somewhat blocky close up. But if you do use Kodi the text and buttons will be plenty large enough from afar.
